incidents.vector: Attackers obtained employee GitHub authentication tokens for SAP's software development environment, enabling them to copy and modify source code.
incidents.impact: SAP confirmed suspicious activity in its GitHub-hosted development infrastructure, restricting access, halting automated builds, and rotating signing keys. The company says it has found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached the Air Force's Cloud One cloud infrastructure platform; the intrusion was discovered during a platform upgrade.
incidents.impact: The breach may have exposed large amounts of sensitive tactical and personnel data. It remains unclear whether data was accessed or who is responsible.

incidents.victim: UK Department for Work and Pensions
incidents.vector: Officials detected a "serious incident" and proactively took systems offline as a precaution; cause not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Systems supporting benefits and pensions for tens of millions of UK residents were taken offline. Officials say payments are unaffected.

incidents.vector: A newly identified group exploits SS7 and Diameter telecom signaling protocol weaknesses to plant backdoors in carrier infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Enables collection of device data, subscriber location tracking, and interception of calls and SMS traffic across multiple carriers; the group, tracked as SilentAir, has been active since early 2025.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a forgotten, unrevoked cloud access key originally issued to a third-party AI service provider, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access.
incidents.impact: Intruder expanded access across Barracuda's internal network and cloud environments for nearly two days earlier in the month before being contained.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeted AFP Forum, the platform media clients use to browse and download AFP's news content.
incidents.impact: AFP took the Forum platform offline as a precaution; it remains unavailable, disrupting content distribution to media organizations worldwide.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack resulted in unauthorized access to personal and business information; a newly launched extortion group calling itself the "Handsome Boy Hacking Club" claimed credit.
incidents.impact: Personal and business data was accessed. FIFA is working with law enforcement; the extortion group's leak site currently lists five victims.

incidents.victim: Cyprus-based airline, telecom, critical infrastructure, and government entities
incidents.vector: A previously undocumented Iranian group, assessed as a likely offshoot of an established Iranian threat group, uses AI-generated phishing lures and a custom backdoor communicating over a decentralized file-sharing network for command and control.
incidents.impact: Intelligence-gathering campaign targeting Cyprus's government, infrastructure, and regional defense relationships; activity has expanded to target Saudi healthcare organizations.

incidents.vector: An unauthorized party gained access to a limited subset of FinCEN systems; the method of intrusion has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The agency took some systems offline, disrupting the BSA E-Filing portal used for anti-money-laundering reporting and extending filer deadlines. No evidence yet of a breach of beneficial-ownership databases; FBI, CISA, and forensic examiners are investigating.

incidents.victim: Japan Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the ministry's government procurement system; the intrusion was detected October 1 but disclosed publicly in late November.
incidents.impact: Potentially exposed about 1,700 email addresses and 164,000 records containing company and employee information tied to government tender bidders. No evidence found so far of public disclosure or misuse.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised an employee GitHub account and used it to push malicious code into 1Password's backend systems.
incidents.impact: Attacker accessed limited account metadata, including usernames, email addresses, and account timestamps. The company says password vaults and secret keys were not accessed or compromised.

incidents.vector: Fake recruiter "take-home assessment" GitHub repositories reference 13 malicious NuGet packages; building the project side-loads a malicious DLL or downloads an executable.
incidents.impact: Payloads steal browser credentials and cookies and establish remote access to developer machines, risking source code, SSH keys, and cloud or registry tokens.

incidents.vector: Data stolen from a shared regional IT provider serving Flemish municipalities; the group is known for automating attacks using an open-weight Chinese AI model.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 1.2 million Flemish citizens stolen; some records are already being sold online.

incidents.victim: CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI)
incidents.vector: Breach of an IT system exposed unclassified data from an open-source intelligence analysis system. Reporting ties the intrusion to the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework, which Microsoft says Chinese state-backed groups have integrated into their toolkits.
incidents.impact: Unclassified data exposed at both the CIA and ODNI, the same day as a separate FinCEN incident; investigators are assessing whether the two are connected.

incidents.victim: Bordeaux University Hospital and France's National Cancer Institute
incidents.vector: At Bordeaux, compromised email accounts were used to send mass phishing emails to employees; an extortion group claimed responsibility and threatened to publish stolen medical records.
incidents.impact: Both organizations are investigating potential theft of medical records, prescriptions, lab results, and financial documents, part of a wider wave of French healthcare cyberattacks this week.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack in September; the Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility.
incidents.impact: May have compromised personal information of more than 11 million customers, business partners, employees, and job applicants.

incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a critical (10/10 severity) untrusted-deserialization zero-day to take over six backend servers.
incidents.impact: No unauthorized modifications found in stored packages, but database reads were not logged, so user data exposure cannot be ruled out. All backend credentials have been rotated.

incidents.vector: Suspected ransomware attack encrypted hospital databases; investigators are examining whether access came through a previously compromised IT supplier.
incidents.impact: Forced postponement of surgeries, suspension of some cancer and radiation treatments, and a shift to paper-based records at the island's largest hospital. Recovery expected to take several days.

incidents.victim: Financial services, healthcare, and legal organizations (US, UK, Australia)
incidents.vector: Com-affiliated actors pose as internal IT support via vishing calls, directing employees to adversary-in-the-middle proxy sites that capture credentials and MFA approvals in real time.
incidents.impact: Sustained data theft and extortion campaign since August 2026; attackers exfiltrate cloud mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint data, then extort victims via internal messages pointing to Tor-hosted negotiation sites.

incidents.victim: Organizations targeted by a financially motivated North Korea-aligned actor
incidents.vector: Threat group tracked as UAT-12643 deploys the Overlord RAT, which embeds encrypted command-and-control server URLs in blockchain transaction memos.
incidents.impact: Blockchain-based command and control removes single points of failure from attacker infrastructure, combined with targeted infostealing to harvest credentials and data.

incidents.vector: Two unauthorized versions of the agent-framework Python package were uploaded to PyPI containing credential-stealing code.
incidents.impact: Any environment that installed the malicious versions should be treated as compromised, requiring full credential rotation. Microsoft's Agent Framework GitHub repository was temporarily taken offline as a precaution.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations including major media, financial, and technology brands
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's account registration process to inject malicious JavaScript into customer experimentation projects, served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN.
incidents.impact: Malicious script skimmed payment card data, swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and attempted to deliver mobile exploit kits to site visitors across at least 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Equifax, and Zoom.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack encrypted data at the largest port in South America, coinciding with a data center power outage of undetermined connection.
incidents.impact: Disrupted the port's ERP systems and customer-facing website and online services; some data created after Oct. 31 was permanently lost despite backup recovery. Services were fully restored Nov. 24, amid a broader surge of ransomware hitting Latin American ports, pipelines, and manufacturers.
